title: ynf factory
description: A factory's configuration repository: .agents/factory/factory.yaml, read from its default branch at a resolved commit (ADR-006). Which repositories ynf works on, and the trackers and forges it works with. Default lanes for every enrolled repository go beside it in lanes.yaml.

repos.description: The enrolled repositories: host/owner/name, or owner/name on the default forge. ynf reads a target repository's lanes only when it is enrolled here.

trackers.description: Tracker instances by name (ADR-003), declared only here: they carry credentials and name servers ynf starts. A reference may use the name (jira/PLAT-881); items are stored by the tracker's host.

provider.description: mcp: a tracker with an MCP server, called directly, with no model.

site.description: The tracker's web address; its host names it in item keys.

server.description: The MCP server: a command that speaks MCP on stdio, or a URL.

command.description: Started with only PATH, HOME and the variables in env.

env.description: ynf's credentials for this tracker, by name, passed to the command.

token_env.description: The variable holding the URL's bearer token.

fields.description: CEL over the get tool's result, bound to result.

repo.description: The repository the ticket names for its code, from a structured field (a label, a component, a custom field), never its text. When set, it must agree with where the code is sent.

closed_when.description: CEL over status and labels: true means the ticket is closed.

forges.description: Forge instances besides the default one, by name (ADR-003), declared only here: a GitHub Enterprise Server beside github.com, say. A repository on one is enrolled as host/owner/name.

provider.description: github: github.com or GitHub Enterprise Server.

url.description: The forge's web address, such as https://github.acme.internal. Its host names the forge in item keys; its API is found from it.

token_env.description: The variable holding ynf's token for this forge, used for its API and its git remotes.

args.description: Its arguments. A string that is exactly {add}, {remove} or {labels} becomes that list; {key} and {text} are replaced inside any string.
